name: analog-synth-chase
style: 1983 analog synthesizer thriller cue, film-score sound design with shouted spoken dialogue, no singing. 150 BPM driving sixteenth-note bass sequence from a monophonic analog synth, low resonance, slightly detuned and unquantised; huge gated-reverb snare cracking on 2 and 4; dark brooding polysynth pads underneath, tape echo; an ambulance siren voiced as a detuned two-tone synth wail sliding over the top. Three panicked voices shout their lines in a British accent over the cue: a rough, smoky young woman screaming; a man speaking low, clipped and fast, then cracking; a driver yelling hoarse and high. Abrupt cut at the red light: the sequence stops dead on one sustained bass note, its filter closing slowly to a dull hum, no drums. A snooty posh male voice heard through a thin, tinny 1980s car phone, petulant. Ending: a single pure electronic sine flatline tone alone, every instrument gone, then dead silence. Dry, close, urgent, midnight rain.
exclude: singing, melody, chorus, rap, choir, upbeat, happy, funk, comedy, synthwave vocals, autotune, guitar solo, fade-out
lyrics:
[Intro: racing synth bass sequence, gated snare, siren wail]

[Shouted, female, screaming]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!

[Spoken fast, male, low and tight]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!

[Shouted, male driver, hoarse]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!

[Break: sequence freezes on one held bass note, filter closing, drums stop]

[Spoken, male, cracking]
Why have we stopped?!

[Spoken, posh man through a tinny car phone]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!

[Whispered, female, quiet]
Fifty over twen—

[Outro: solo flatline sine tone, no music]

[Silence]

[End]
